messages:
maria: Hey team, customer reporting sudden 401s after they switched their client from dev -> prod org. Says the same API key worked earlier today. They pasted a curl and response. Can someone triage? :eyes:

jason: Can you paste the exact curl (with key redacted) and the raw response body + headers? Also need x-request-id if present.

maria: Paste below (key replaced with <KEY>):

```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: req_20230315_9f3a2b

{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}

maria: They said they copied the key from the dashboard while toggled into the dev org, then used it against the prod client. Customer is small fintech so they maybe have org-scoped keys.

ingrid: Ok that smells like an org-scoped key. We have two mechanisms that can cause 401s: key rotation/expiry or key-scoped-to-org/environment. If they copied from dev org UI and then used in prod request, the platform rejects it.

jason: To confirm: ask them to run `GET /v1/keys/<KEY_ID>` via the dashboard API (or check the key metadata in the console) and confirm the "scopes" and "bound_org" fields. If they can't, ask for the key id (not the secret) or the last 6 chars.

maria: Customer sent last 6 chars: "...pQ9z7". Can someone look up?

ingrid: Looking in admin tooling now. Found active key with id k_32f... bound_org: dev-team-acme. Scope: hosted:read, hosted:write. Not valid for prod-team-acme org. That will return invalid_api_key when used against prod account.

jason: That matches. Root cause: org-bound key used across org boundary. Action: create a prod-scoped key or issue an org-agnostic service key if customer needs cross-org. Also check if the user intended to use a dedicated/deploy key — those keys are separate.

maria: What's the recommended quick fix I should send the customer?

ingrid: Two options: 1) From their prod org console, create a new API key and use that in prod client (fastest). 2) If they need one key for both, ask SRE to create a platform service key with multi-org binding (requires approval). For immediate unblock, option 1.

jason: Also send them this repro command to test with a prod-scoped key (replace <PROD_KEY>):

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <PROD_KEY>" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```
If response is 200 they are unblocked. If 401 persists, capture x-request-id and send to us.

maria: I told the customer to create a prod key and test. They came back: prod key works, they can generate. They asked why the dashboard copy didn't warn about org scope.

ingrid: Good catch. We should add a small UI hint when copying keys that are org-scoped ("This key is bound to dev-team-acme and will not work in other orgs"). Please create a small UX ticket.

jason: Filed FE ticket FE-8342 to show scope badge + copy tooltip. Added acceptance: if key.bound_org != current_org show :lock: "Scoped to {bound_org}" when copying.

maria: Customer satisfied, reauth solved. Closing ticket but leaving note for docs.

ops-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026 created from thread by maria. Priority: P2.

maria: I'll follow up with short doc snippet and reply to customer with remediation steps + link to docs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jason: Optional: check audit logs to ensure there was no attempted cross-org exploitation. I scanned a couple requests and they look like legitimate dev->prod test attempts. No further action. :white_check_mark:

maria: Closing thread in 24h unless customer reopens.
